comments.content: Moving the fixed blue from a *container* colour (white label on a blue fill) to a *content* colour breaks legibility on dark dialog surfaces. `KomiDialog` paints on `personality.colors.surface` (manga: panel, classic dark: `#1A1C1E`), so `#3B5BDB` ends up at roughly **1.8:1** on the Manga NORD panel (`#3B4252`) and **~3.0:1** on the classic dark/AMOLED surfaces — far below the 4.5:1 the codebase targets for body text (`MIN_BODY_CONTRAST` in `personality/model/ColorContrast.kt`). Previously this was safe only because the blue was the fill and the label was white (5.7:1 everywhere). The repo already has a helper for exactly this (used in `MangaButtonRoles`), so route the preferred blue through `ensureContrast` (needs `import zed.rainxch.core.presentation.personality.model.ensureContrast`); alternatively keep the filled blue treatment.

containerColor = Color.Transparent,
                            // Stays blue on light surfaces, falls back to legible ink on dark ones.
                            contentColor =
                                ensureContrast(
                                    preferred = Color(0xFF3B5BDB),
                                    background = personality.colors.surface,
                                    ink = personality.colors.onSurface,
                                    page = personality.colors.background,
                                ),

"Switching the fixed blue from a *container* colour (white label on a blue fill) to a *content* colour makes the label unreadable on dark dialog surfaces: the dialog renders on `personality.colors.surface`, so `#3B5BDB` ends up at ~1.8:1 on the Manga NORD panel (#3B4252) and ~3.0:1 on the classic dark surface (#1A1C1E) — well under the 4.5:1 the codebase targets for body text (see `MIN_BODY_CONTRAST` in ColorContrast.kt). The same fixed blue was safe before because it was paired with white content. Consider keeping the blue as a fill, or pass the preferred blue through `ensureContrast(..., personality.colors.surface, personality.colors.onSurface, personality.colors.background)` so it stays blue on light themes and falls back to legible ink on dark ones."

So the blue on dark themes becomes near-white, losing the blue meaning, but gains legibility. That's the codebase's own established behavior pattern.

comments.content: Same concern as the blue label, but for the other button and with a different root cause: the Manga error palettes are tuned as *container* colours (they are paired with `onError` for text on an error fill — see `MangaColors.paperInk`, e.g. NORD `error = 0xFFE5818A` + `onError = 0xFF20242E`), not as text on the Manga panel surface. On Manga NORD the dialog paints `colors.surface = 0xFF3B4252`, so `0xFFE5818A` lands at only ≈3.8:1 for this 12sp label (below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for text of that size; DAY/NIGHT/cobalt are fine). Also note the override path returns `contentColor` verbatim and skips KomiButton's internal `ensureContrast`, so nothing corrects it. Consider passing a contrast-checked error tone, e.g. `ensureContrast(personality.colors.error, personality.colors.surface, personality.colors.onSurface, personality.colors.surface)` (needs an import from `zed.rainxch.core.presentation.personality.model`), or keep the destructive fill so the label sits on `error`/`onError`.
